claim: Under the January 2025 due-diligence rule, a front-end fabricator or OSAT exporting a logic IC made at the 16/14 nm node or below (or with a non-planar transistor architecture) must presume it is ECCN 3A090.a unless (a) an approved or authorised designer attests it is not, or (b) the front-end fabricator (if packaging outside Macau/D:5) or an approved OSAT attests the packaged IC has fewer than 30 billion transistors, or has no HBM and fewer than 35 billion (exports completed in 2027) or 40 billion (2029 or later) transistors.
evidence: "b. If the integrated circuit die is packaged by the ``front-end fabricator'' at a location outside of Macau or a destination specified in Country Group D:5 ..., then the attestation of the ``front-end fabricator'' that (a) the ``aggregated approximated transistor count'' of the final packaged IC is below 30 billion transistors, or (b) the final packaged IC does not contain high-bandwidth memory and that the ``aggregated approximated transistor count'' of the final packaged IC is below (i) 35 billion transistors for any exports, reexports, or transfers (in-country) completed in 2027; or (ii) 40 billion transistors for any exports, reexports, or transfers (in-country) completed in 2029 or thereafter" (90 FR 5298, Note 1 to 3A090.a, FR p. 5314); "Applicable advanced logic integrated circuits are logic integrated circuits produced using the ``16/14 nanometer node'' or below, or using a non-planar transistor architecture." (772.1, FR p. 5313-14)

metric.name: Transistor-count threshold to overcome 3A090.a presumption
metric.unit: billion transistors (aggregated approximated count, final packaged IC; with or without HBM)
metric.population: Final packaged applicable advanced logic ICs; HBM-free ICs may use 35bn (exports completed in 2027) or 40bn (2029 or later)

notes: Corrects CLM-0863: the no-HBM condition applies only to the 35bn/40bn thresholds. The text sets no distinct 2028 threshold.

claim: Under the January 2025 rule (15 CFR 743.9), front-end fabricators producing ICs specified or presumed to be specified in ECCN 3A090.a for authorised (non-approved) IC designers must submit quarterly reports to BIS including a Know Your Customer vetting form, with the first report due 31 May 2025; the reporting duty does not apply to OSATs.
evidence: "``Front-end fabricators'' producing any integrated circuit specified under ECCN 3A090.a or presumed to be specified under ECCN 3A090.a by Note 1 to 3A090 for any authorized integrated circuit designer must submit reports to BIS in accordance with this section."; "(3) The end-user Know Your Customer (KYC) vetting form included in supplement no. 2 of this part"; "(c) Quarterly reporting requirement. (1) You must submit the first report by May 31, 2025." (90 FR 5298, 15 CFR 743.9, FR p. 5310)
notes: Corrects CLM-0865, which put the reporting duty on OSATs too. 'Does not apply to OSATs' is our reading: 743.9 names only front-end fabricators.

claim: As of September 2026, 15 CFR 744.6(c)(2) requires US persons to have a licence to ship, transmit, transfer, facilitate or service items not subject to the EAR to or within Macau or Country Group D:5 when they will be used for IC development or production at facilities of Macau/D:5-headquartered entities producing advanced-node ICs, and, regardless of end use, for items meeting specified SME ECCNs (3B001.a.4, c, d, f.1, f.5, f.6, k to n, p.2, p.4, r, 3B002.c, 3D992, 3E992).
evidence: "(i) 'Development' or 'production' of 'advanced-node ICs.' To or within Macau or a destination specified in Country Group D:5, any item not subject to the EAR that you know will be used in the 'development' or 'production' of integrated circuits at a 'facility' of an entity headquartered in, or whose ultimate parent company is headquartered in, either Macau or a destination specified in Country Group D:5 where 'production' of 'advanced-node integrated circuits' occurs"; "(iii) Semiconductor manufacturing equipment. To or within either Macau or a destination specified in Country Group D:5, any item not subject to the EAR and meeting the parameters of ECCNs 3B001.a.4, c, d, f.1, f.5, f.6, k to n, p.2, p.4, r, 3B002.c, 3D992, or 3E992 regardless of end use or end user." (15 CFR 744.6(c)(2), eCFR as of 2026-09-01)
notes: Supersedes the October 2022 wording in CLM-0868 (PRC-only, ECCN 3B090). Paragraph (c)(2)(ii) also covers Category 3 B-E items where production of ICs occurs but advanced-node status is unknown. Amended by 88 FR 73448/73494, 89 FR 23885, 89 FR 96817 and 90 FR 5311.

claim: As of September 2026, licence applications under the US-persons restriction in 15 CFR 744.6(c)(2) face a presumption of denial for Macau and Country Group D:5 destinations and for entities headquartered (or with ultimate parents headquartered) there, with case-by-case review for other applications; review factors include technology level, customers, compliance plans and contract sanctity.
evidence: "License review will take into account factors including technology level, customers, compliance plans, and contract sanctity. (i) Presumption of denial. Applications will be reviewed with a presumption of denial for Macau and destinations specified in Country Group D:5 and entities headquartered or whose ultimate parent is headquartered in Macau or destinations specified in Country Group D:5, unless paragraph (e)(3)(ii) of this section applies. (ii) Case-by-case. ... (C) For all other applications not specified in paragraph (e)(3)(i) or (e)(3)(ii)(A) or (B) of this section." (15 CFR 744.6(e)(3), eCFR as of 2026-09-01)
notes: Supersedes the October 2022 policy in CLM-0869. Case-by-case exceptions (e)(3)(ii)(A)-(B) cover certain 3A090/4A090 and .z items not for datacentres, and cases where a foreign-available equivalent exists.
